instructions:
1. Place a dumbbell on each side of your body and stand between them.
2. Squat down, grip both dumbbells, and stand up with arms straight at your sides.
3. Brace your core, lift your chest, and pull your shoulders back.
4. Walk forward in short controlled steps with an upright torso.
5. At the end of the set distance, turn around and walk back.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso tall and avoid leaning forward or to either side.
2. Squeeze the handles hard to keep your grip secure.
3. Take steady, even steps and do not rush.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the carry.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms touch the floor.
5. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Move slowly and under control to keep tension on the chest.
3. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
4. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
3. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Control the lowering phase to protect your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Slowly squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Use a slow tempo on both the lowering and lifting phases.
3. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
4. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.

instructions:
1. Set a bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline and sit back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Squeeze your upper chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
3. Keep your back against the bench and your shoulders pulled down.
4. Control the lowering phase to protect your shoulders.
